full_judgment:
Abdul Wadud Choudhury, J.—This Rule arises out of an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and is directed against an order dated 23.11.79 passed by the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Industries under Motivation No. Ind/AA-2/111, 3/79/382 (Annexure N) by which it was stated that the petitioner was an Inspector of explosives on probation and was holding the charge of Chief Inspector of Explosives in addition to his own duties and not promoted to that post and as such he should be treated and addressed as Inspector of Explosives in charge for all purposes including Official Correspondence. That notification also illegally stated that the appointment of the petitioner as an Inspector of Explosives was to be reviewed on the basis of the records in terms of Section 11(2) of the President's Order No. 34/72 as he was appointed to that post on 1.8.71. 

 2. The facts relevant for the purpose of the Rule are to the effect that the petitioner was appointed as Assistant Inspector of Explosives (Class II gazetteer post) on 1.8.67 on selenium and recommendation of the Central Public Service Commission under the then Government of Pakistan and thereafter he was appointed on the recommendation of the Central Public Service Commission to be appointed as Inspector of Explosives on 1.8.71. and in that capacity he served the department until 30.6.72. Again on 4.7.72 the petitioner was appointed as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives by Notification No. 2L3/72/246 and he assumed charge as the Deputy Inspector of Explosives from 1st of July, 1972. The petitioner relinquished the post Inspector of Explosives with effect from 19.7.72 after making over charge of the post of Inspector of Explosives, Khulna to an Assistant inspector of Explosives who had been transferred there as Inspector-in-Charge from Dacca by the Ministry of Industries and Natural Resources. The Notification, according to the petitioner clearly indicated that the petitioner was made the Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives until further orders though he was not confirmed in the rank of Inspector of Explosives. After the reorganization of the Department of Explosives a new set-up in the said Department under the Ministry of Industries (Industries Division) was created and it was stated that the said new set-up will come into force with immediate effect. Under the said new set-up the post of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives was redesign Ted as Chief Inspector of Explosives and the said post was made Class I Senior Post. Under the said arrangement three posts of Inspectors of Explosives Class 1 Junior were created, one for Dacca. one for Chittagong and the third one for Khulna and three Assistant Inspectors of Explosives Class II were also created in the new set-up, one for Dacca, one for Chittagong and one for Khulna. This setup was intimated to the Ministry of Finance as also to the Accountant General, Bangladesh and a copy, of the same was sent for information to the petitioner under the following beading "Copy forwarded to the Ministry of Finance for information and communication to the Accountant General, Bangladesh, Dacca. Copy forwarded for Information to Chief Inspector of Explosives, Ex-Central Secretariat. Segunbagicha, Dacca. He is requested to absorb the present Technical Assistant in a suitable post in the Department of Explosives due to abolition of the post of Technical Assistant in the set-up. The Petitioner contends that while he was continuing as the Chief Inspector and drawing his pay according to his new sale as Chief inspector for quite a long time the respondent No 3 became annoyed with him for not giving effect to certain illegal orders of the respondent No. 3. Thereafter the respondent No. 3 issued an order of suspension against the petitioner by Order dated 13.12.77 by Memo. No. AA-I/Con-4/77/341 on charges of inefficiency, misconduct and corruption. As against the said order of suspension, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 722/77 in the First Court of Munsif, Dacca against respondent Nos. 1-3 as defendents for a declaration that the said suspension order was illegal, ultra-vires, void, malafide, inoperative and not binding on the petitioner. The respondent Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing joint written statement. The learned Munsif by his judgment and decree dated 30.6.78 decreed the suit with the finding that the order of suspension of the petitioner from the post of Chief Inspector of Explosives, Bangladesh Dacca by the respondent No. 3 was illegal, uliravires, void, malafide, inoperative and not binding. As against the judgment and decree, the respondent Nos. 1-3 preferred an appeal before the learned District judge and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dacca after hearing both the parties dismissed the appeal on 10.4.79 and affirmed the Judgment and decree of the trial court. In the meantime, the President's Co-ordination and Control Cell for National Security held a thorough enquiry against the petitioner on certain allegations, one of which was drawls of pay of the post of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives without promotion from the post of Inspector. The enquiry was held on all allegations and the same were found to be baseless and it was found in the said enquiry that the petitioner was promoted to the rank of Deputy Chief Inspector until further orders as also that he was held by the Civil Court to hold the post of Chief inspector and the appointment letter also proved the Canine and as such the Co-ordination and Control Cell recommended that the petitioner be allowed to join to the post of Chief inspector of Explosives treating his period of suspension as on duty. Thereafter the respondent No. 1 directed the respondent No. 3 to allow the petitioner to join his duties ; but the respondent No. 3 by Notification No. Ind/AA-1/4M-64 79 dated 14-7-79 while withdrawing the suspension order, ordered that the petitioner sboulcrbe treated as inspector of explosives holding the charge of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives with effect from 1-7-72. The petitioner did not join the department on protest since the said order virtually purported to have reduced the rank, salary and other amenities of the petitioner and the said order being against the Civil Court's verdict and the direction of the respondent No. 1. He filed an application on 16-7-79 for withdrawal of the aforesaid Notification and to allow him to join in the post of Chief Inspector of Explosives. On receipt of the said representation of the petitioner, the respondent No. 2 issued a fresh Notification No. Ind/AA-1/4M-/64/79/766 dated 4-8-79 canceling the Notification issued by respondent No. 3 and withdrew the suspension order and allowed the petitioner to join as Chief Inspector of Explosives. A copy of the said letter was also sent to the petitioner addressing him as Chief Inspector of Explosives. Thereafter the petitioner submitted his joining report on 15-8-79 and since then he has been working in the Department of Ex-plosives. as Chief Inspector of Explosives. The respondent No. 3 again defying the notification dated 4-8-79 issued on 18-8-79 the letter No. Sec.-AA-1/4M-64/79-Ind/154(A) intimating the Accountant General of Bangladesh to treat the petitioner as Inspector of. Explosives. The petitioner protested against the said letter by letter No. 1(250)/II dated 9.11.79. The Ministry of Industries issued letter No. Ind/AA-2/IR-3/79 dated 16-11-79 addressing to the respondent No. 4 the Accountant General (Civil) of Bangladesh, intimating him that the suspension order of the petitioner as Chief Inspector has been with-drawn and to allow him to draw his salary in the scale Tk. 750-75-1500/- as the pay he was drawing before his suspension. A copy of the some was given to the petitioner addressing him as the Chief Inspector of Ex-plosives. In the meantime, a departmental proceeding was drawn against the petitioner on the charges of inefficiency, misconduct and corruption and the Deputy Secretary (Enq.), Establishment Division, Ministry of Cabinet Affairs was appointed Enquiry Officer by the Secretary of the Ministry of Industries The said Officers after enquiry found the petitioner not guilty of the charges of inefficiency, misconduct and corruption and re-commended on 30-1-80 that the petitioner be exonerated of all the charges leveled against him. In spite of all these, the respondent No. 3 issued notification No. Indy/ AA-2/IR-3/79/382 dated 23-11-79 directing all concerned to treat and address the petitioner for all purposes including official correspondence as Inspector of Explosives with the remark that the appointment of the petitioner would be reviewed u/s. 11(2) of the President's Order No. 34/72 though the same was repealed long ago and his appointment was made on 1-8-71. But this was not taken notice of while the impugned order was passed. The petitioner requested the respondents to cancel the said order in view of the fact that since the petitioner was promoted to the post of Chief Inspector he could not be addressed or re-designated as Inspector of Explosives. He also intimated that the case of the petitioner was reviewed as far back as on 12-5-72 and in view of the review no question of another fresh review did arise. In view of the said notification the petitioner's pay as Chief Inspector was not being allowed to be drawn. Since the petitioner was not given any reply to his representation with regard to the said order he has filed this application and obtained the present Rule. This Rule was contested by the respondent No. 1, the Government and respondent No. 3, the Deputy Secretary Mr. Shahidul Huq Khan who passed the impugned order by filing two separate affidavits-in-opposition. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 1, it has been stated that the petitioner was appointed an Inspector of Explosives and while he was acting as such in a temporary cadre the post of Deputy Chief Inspector fell vacant and the petitioner was asked to hold the current charge in addition to his duties. It has been stated them that the petitioner has not been treated as Chief Inspector in any way and as such he could not as of right claim that he hp been promoted to the post of Chief Inspector of Explosives and he has no legal right to the said post of Chief Inspector of Explosives as his Case was not seam of promotion. The respondent No. 3 filed affidavit-in-opposition contending that he had no malade or malice in the matter of passing the notifies ton issued under his signature. He has issued the same under the orders of his superiors. He has further submitted that the findings against him in the enquiry report of the Co-ordination and Central Cell as also of the Court are not based on record and these observations have been .made without any reference to him. 

 4. Mr. Paul, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the letter appointing the petitioner as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives, the Annexure B together with Annexure C and the judgment and the Civil Court Annexure F and Annexure Z, the judgment of the Appellate Court together with Annexures I and L categorically and unmistakably proved that the petitioner's appointment as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives was a promotion and he was holding the post since 1-7-72 until further orders and as such he could not now be termed as Inspector of Explosives holding the charge of the Office of the Chief Inspector of Explosives in addition to his own duties and the said order must be found to be without any lawful authority. He further submits that after the petitioner was appointed as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives he handed over charge of his Office as Inspector to another person and this, handing over of charge of his substantive post would definitely show that he was not holding the charge of the Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives in addition to his own duties. In that view Mr. Paul submits that this Notification, Annexure N. issued by the respondent No. 3 cannot be sustained. The Attorney General, on the other band, contends that Annexure B, the appointment letter read with Annexure C do not prove that the petitioner was promoted. He submits that Annexure B, the letter by which the petitioner was given charge together with the conduct of the petitioner as stated in paragraph 10 of the affidavit-in-opposition as also paragraph 3 of the affidavit filed by the petitioner, would tend to show that the petitioner was for all practical purposes an Inspector of Explosives and was not appointed as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives and has no substantive appointment as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives. Moreover, he submits that the petitioner has not been able to show that his case was considered by the Public Service Commission in the matter of appointment as Deputy Chief Inspector redesign Ted as Chief Inspector of Explosives and as such he could not be said to hold the substantive rank of Chief Inspector of Explosives. He further submits that the Civil Court decrees are only with regard to suspension order passed against the petitioner and the question as to whether the petitioner is Chief Inspector or Deputy Chief Inspector has not been gone into and was not the subject matter in issue. The learned Attorney General further submits that on a proper consideration of Annexure B it will he found there the petitioner was never appointed as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives. He was only ordered to hold current charges until further orders. He further submits that were fact of holding of charge by the incumbent for a long period would not give him any right to the post. In support of his contention he has relied on the case of Shamsul Alam vs. Superintendent of Police; Bangladesh Railway and others reported in 33 DLR (AD) 100 wherein it has been stated that officiating for any length of time does not confer on a person any substantive right. On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case it is abundantly clear that the petitioner was promoted to the post of Deputy Chief Inspector on and from 1.7.72. The order was to the following effect: 

 We also find the enquiry report of the Co-ordination and Control Cell that after the appointment of the petitioner as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives he handed over charge of his office to another Officer and was relieved of his duties as Inspector of Explosives and joined the post of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives. The petitioner was not transferred to join here as Inspector of Explosives and to hold the current charges of the Deputy Chief Inspector. Here we are to consider the character of the appointment and considering the same we hold that the petitioner was not holding the charge of the post of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives but he was the whole time appointee in the said post. He relinquished his Office as Inspector of Explosives with effect from 19.7.72 as we find from page 43 of the petition (Annexure) and from this it cannot be said that the petitioner was merely holding charge of the Office in addition to his post as Inspector of Explosives. We also find from Annexure C that there was a reorganisation of the Department of Explosives and the post of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives was re-designated as Chief Inspector of Explosives and there were three posts of Inspectors and three posts of Assistant Inspectors. The petitioner continued in the post as the Chief Inspector of Explosives in all purposes. Since the re-organisation the Department of Explosives dated 20.10.72, the petitioner is continuing to hold the said post of Chief Inspector and for all purposes he was being recognised as snob by the Government, Annexure I, dated 4.6.79. By this letter the suspension order passed by the respondent No. 3 on behalf of the Ministry against the petitioner was withdrawn and the letter was written to the petitioner as Chief Inspector of Explosives. Next, we come to another letter dated 16.11.79 written by the Section Officer of the Government of Bangladesh, Ministry of Industries in a controversy as to his drawal of pay as Chief Inspector. The respondent No. 3 intimated the Accountant General to the fact that the petitioner was not a Chief Inspector of Explosives and as such his pay should be in accordance with the pay admissible to that as an Inspector. He was also holding charge of the Office of the Chief Inspector. As against said letter, the petitioner protested to the Government and the Government by the letter, Annexure L, dated 16.11.79 held to the following effect: 

 "I am directed to refer to this Ministry's order No, AA-1/Con-4/77/341 dt. 13.12.77 suspending Mr. M. A. Rashid, Chief Inspector of Explosives in Bangladesh, Dacca has already been with-drawn by this Ministry's notification No. Ind/AA-1/4M-64/79/766 dt, 4.8.79 & subsequent modified endorsement No. Ind/AA-1/4M-64/79/151 13.8.79 and accordingly. Mr, M. A. Rashid has joined his duties in the Department of Explosives w.e.f. 15.8.79 (forenoon). I am also directed to convey the sanction of the govt. to allow Mr. M. A. Rashid to draw his salary in the scale of pay he had been drawing be-fore suspension, after fixation of pay by the A.G.B. This supersedes all previous orders-issued in respect of drawls of his pay by this Ministry." This letter was addressed to the Accountant General (Civil) of Bangladesh. A copy of this letter was sent to the petitioner as Chief Inspector of Explosives in Bangladesh, In spite of this a notification was issued by the respondent No. 3 and copy was given to the Accountant General of Bangladesh and others and this notification was to the following effect : 

 "Whereas, Mr. M. A. Rashid, Inspector of Explosives on probation was given the charge of the office of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives (redesign Ted as Chief Inspector of Explosives) w.e.f. 1.7.72 in addition to his own duties and not promoted to that post in terms of this ministry's notification No. 2L/3/72/246 dated 4.7.72 and therefore, he would be treated and addressed as Inspector of Explosives in-charge for all purposes including official correspondence. 

 5. On a consideration of the Annexure that have been filed in the present case we do not find any basis for the said notification by which it is stated that the petitioner was holding his Office as Chief Inspector of Explosives in addition to his own duties. As we have found earlier, the petitioner was appointed as the Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives while he was serving as Inspector of Explosives at Khulna and thereafter he handed over charge as Inspector of Explosives of Khulna and joined his post as Deputy Chief Inspector at Dacca. After he handed over charge, he was no longer an Inspector of Explosives but assumed charge of Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives and became whole time incumbent in the said post. As such it could not be said that he was holding charge of the Office of the Deputy Chief Inspector in addition to his own duties. The appointment letter Annexure B does not give any such indication. In, that view of the matter, it could not be said that this notification passed by the respondent No. 3 can be sustained. With regard to the contention of the learned Attorney General that since the petitioner was only holding the charge and not appointed substantively as Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives, he had no right to challenge this notification since he has not been substantively appointed to the post. We do not think that this contention of the learned Attorney General is tenable in the facts and circumstances of the case. With regard to the question that since his service was not regularized by referring the same to the Public Service Commission he could be deemed to be lawfully appointed as Chief Inspector of Explosive and he has referred to Article 140 of the Constitution and has submitted that without consulting the Public Service Commission no such appointment could be made. On a reading of Article 140 together with Article 141, however, we find that an appointment can be made even without consulting the Public Service Commission. An appointment without reference to the Public Service Commission will not be bad if the government failed to refer the matter to the Public Service Commission at the time of making the appointment and this question cannot be raised after such a long period of nine or ten years. The Government cannot now raise the plea that the appointment cannot be regarded as valid in view of the fact that the matter has not been referred to the Public Service Commission. The respondent No. I cannot take the shelter of their own lathes and lapses. It will be seen that the petitioner was appointed as whole time Deputy Chief Inspector of Explosives front 1.7.72 and subsequently predesignated as Chief Inspector of Explosives from 20.10.72 in which post he is carrying on till date. So, applying the case of Government of Bangladesh vs. Md. Ismail Hossein reported in 31 DLR (AD) 127 as also the principle enunciated in the case of Abdul Majid Sheikh vs. Mushoffe Ahmed & ors. reported in 17 DLR (SC) 63 we find that the petitioner having continued indefinitely in duration of time as Chief Inspector of Explosives, he could not be reverted to the post of Inspector of Explosives without asking him to show cause for such reduction under Article 135 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Mr. Kazi Shafiuddin, learned Assistant Attorney General, has cited certain decisions reported in PLD 1959(SC) 107 and PLD 1959(SC) 91. We, however, think that these decisions do not apply to the facts and circumstances of the present case. In that view of the matter, we find and hold that the impugned notification dated 23.11.79 contained in Annexure N is illegal and has been made without lawful authority and as such is of no legal effect.
